title: Impossible by Degrees: Cohomology & Bistable Visual Paradox
summary: The Penrose triangle, staircase, and related ``impossible objects'' have long been understood as related to first cohomology $H^1$: the obstruction to extending locally consistent interpretations around a loop. This paper develops a cohomological hierarchy for a class of visual paradoxes. Restricting to systems built from \emph{bistable} elements -- components admitting exactly two local states, such as the Necker cube's forward/backward orientations, a gear's clockwise/counterclockwise spin, or a rhombic tiling corner's convex/concave interpretation -- allows the use of $\mathbb{Z}_2$…
